content.comment_body: Hello, I have a question regarding two references: [article_no] and [article_no]. They seem to be modules, with one providing two analog inputs and the other two analog outputs. I'm unsure how to connect analog input sensors so their values can be output to another module, which lacks analog inputs. Thank you. (Translated with Google)
What kind of information is this? In [product_name], I'm not familiar with modules [article_no] or [article_no].
I found this, but does it work with [product_name]? I saw in the [document] that it should. Thank you.

You've listed dealer article numbers. How are we supposed to decipher what you mean? The module referenced is for analog input to evaluate PT100/1000 resistors. The official article number from [company_name] is [article_no].

Sorry, here are the [company_name] references: [article_no] and [article_no]. To clarify: I need to capture signals from two sensors (speed and temperature), so two analog inputs, and I want to display these values, requiring two analog outputs. Originally, I considered using [article_no] ([product_name] display), but I hadn't noticed its lack of analog inputs, so I looked for other modules. I couldn't find any with both two analog inputs and two analog outputs. Thank you.

You need one [product_name] base module and one analog expansion module ([article_no]), which supports two channels of 0-10V or 0/4-20mA, and one RTD analog expansion module ([article_no]) for PT100/1000 sensors. I'm unclear why you think an analog output module ([article_no]) is required. Could you explain your reasoning? If you're just displaying values on the display panel, you don't need an analog output module.
Hello, apologies for any confusion. I tried to simplify my request. My main issue is understanding how analog information is sent to a display without using an analog output module. Thank you.
If you're referring to the built-in display or the [product_name] display panel, it's simple. You can show the values within a message text. Would you like an example?
Yes, an example would be helpful, if possible. Thank you.
Please see the attached file.

After reviewing your example, I realize my misunderstanding relates more to cabinet wiring. What I don't get is how analog information can be transmitted without an analog output. If I connect the output of the [product_name] software module, will this still retain the analog signal? Thank you.
Your questions are unclear. Please describe exactly what you want to achieve. You mention sending analog data without an analog output module—where do you wish to send it?

Hello, I'd like to understand how the module [article_no] with two analog inputs can send data from two sensors (temperature and speed) to a [product_name] display (when connected in a switchboard). I hope this clarifies my question.
This is demonstrated in the example file I provided.

Hello, I'm not asking how to wire it in the program, but rather how to connect it physically in the electrical cabinet. I don't understand how analog information is transmitted if there are only analog inputs. Thank you.
I'm sorry, but I'm having trouble understanding your question. Perhaps another user can assist.

Hello [user_name], If you want to display signals from two analog inputs (including expansion modules) on a display panel, you don't require any analog outputs. It may be a translation issue causing misunderstanding. Please refer to the manual ([url]) as a PDF; it's free and should address your questions. Best regards, [user_name] (Translated with Google)
Have you reviewed all posts in this thread? It seems not. Your comments are not new.

Hello, sorry for the late reply. I still don't fully understand. My issue now is figuring out how the API [article_no] can receive analog information from the module. Apologies, I forgot to mention this reference earlier.
I'm having difficulty with your description, as you aren't using punctuation. The display panel only shows message texts you create in the program.

I've written the program, but I don't understand how to work with a controller [article_no] and use the analog module [article_no] for analog data. Should I simply wire a digital output to a digital input to use analog signals?
To read values from an analog input module, use the "Analog Input" block to read, and then "Analog Amplifier" to scale the values. You can see this in my example.

Thank you. So, to clarify, I need to implement what you described and program it accordingly? Should I wire digital outputs to digital inputs as you suggest? Also, if my speed sensor reads 100 rpm, should I use the analog amplifier for that?
I'm sorry, but I'm unable to understand your questions. You mention analog modules but then refer to digital connections. I don't see the relationship.

That's exactly my issue. I can't figure out how a controller with 8 digital inputs and outputs can process analog information from a module with 2 analog inputs and 2 digital outputs. Unless connecting one of the digital outputs to the controller allows analog data usage, I don't understand. Thanks for your patience.
I'm getting more confused. There's no expansion module with 2 analog inputs and 2 digital outputs. Sorry, but I can't follow your questions.
Regarding reference [article_no], it lists 2 analog inputs but does not mention outputs, so I assumed perhaps it's digital.
There are digital expansion modules and analog expansion modules, but none feature both analog and digital inputs or outputs together.
Alright, that clears up one issue. Now, how do I connect a module with analog outputs (from two sensors) to a controller that only accepts digital inputs?
Are you asking how to hook up an analog expansion module to a [product_name] base module?
Yes, and I would like to have readings from two sensors (speed and temperature) inside the program.
See attachment for how to install expansion modules. For programming instructions, check my example.
Thanks, just one more question: Regarding output numbering, which comes first? Is it always the module furthest left?
Numbering is from right to left. This is fixed and can't be adjusted.
Okay, thanks for all your help.

analysis.insight_summary: New users to the [product_name] environment often misunderstand hardware module features, particularly thinking analog outputs are needed only to display analog input values on a display. This shows a need for clearer product documentation and basic educational resources about how signals flow and are displayed.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect explicit instructions on which hardware modules are necessary to read analog sensor data and show it on an operator panel. They assume analog output modules are a requirement for display purposes and seek simple, step-by-step guidance.
